q: 401. An advantage of ozone over chlorine for disinfection is it (ozone) ............
options: leaves sufficient chemical to guard against post contamination
explain: Ozone acts as a strong oxidizing agent that can improve the taste and odor of water by breaking down organic compounds, whereas chlorine can sometimes leave a medicinal taste.

q: 402. A disadvantage of ozone is ............
options: impurities are oxidized before disinfection commences
toxic end products are given out
explain: Ozone is highly unstable and has a very short half-life, meaning it must be generated on-site and cannot provide a residual disinfecting effect in the distribution system.

q: 403. Ultra violet rays are highly effective for disinfection for ............
explain: UV rays must physically penetrate the water to strike microorganisms. Turbidity or suspended solids shield bacteria from the light, so UV is only highly effective in clear water.

q: 404. An advantages of ultraviolet radiation is ............
options: it can be used for any type of water
no chemical is added to water
explain: UV disinfection is a physical process rather than a chemical one. This means it doesn't change the chemical composition of the water or add potentially harmful byproducts.

q: 405. An undesirable gas in domestic water is ............
explain: Hydrogen Sulphide (H2S) is highly undesirable because it gives water a 'rotten egg' smell and can be corrosive to plumbing.

q: 406. Fluorides are removed from water by ............
explain: Activated alumina is a common adsorbent used in the 'Nalgonda Technique' or standalone filters specifically to remove excess fluoride from drinking water.

q: 407. Iron and manganese can be removed from water by ............
explain: Oxidation (often through aeration or chemical addition) converts soluble iron and manganese into insoluble forms that can then be removed by filtration.

q: 408. Absolutely soft waters ............
options: cause no damage to pipe line
give lather with synthetic detergent soap
explain: Soft water contains very little calcium and magnesium, which are the primary minerals responsible for forming hard scale (boiler scale) when water is heated.

q: 409. Besides calcium and magnesium, hardness is also caused because of salts of ............
explain: While Ca and Mg are the main culprits, polyvalent metallic cations like Strontium (Sr2+), Iron, and Manganese also contribute to total hardness.

q: 410. Soft waters have a hardness of ............
explain: Water is generally classified as 'soft' if the hardness (as CaCO3) is between 0 and 75 mg/l.

q: 411. Hardness is removed from water based on the relative insolubility of the following ............
explain: In the lime-soda process, calcium is precipitated as Calcium Carbonate (CaCO3) and magnesium is precipitated as Magnesium Hydroxide (Mg(OH)2) due to their low solubility at high pH.

q: 412. The solubility of CaCO3 in pure water at 20°C is ............
explain: The theoretical solubility of calcium carbonate in pure water at standard room temperature is approximately 17 mg/l.

q: 413. The solubility of Mg(OH)2 in pure water at 20°C is ............
explain: Magnesium hydroxide is even less soluble than calcium carbonate, with a solubility of about 9 mg/l at 20°C.

q: 414. CaCO3 gets precipitated at a pH of ............
explain: To effectively remove carbonate hardness, the pH must be raised to around 9.5 to allow Calcium Carbonate to settle out.

q: 415. Mg(OH)2 gets precipitated at a pH of ............
explain: Magnesium removal requires a much higher alkalinity; it typically begins to precipitate effectively only when the pH reaches approximately 11.

q: 416. Carbonate hardness is due to ............
explain: Carbonate hardness (temporary hardness) is primarily caused by the bicarbonates and carbonates of calcium and magnesium.

q: 417. The effluent from the lime soda process contains a hardness of ............
explain: Unlike the zeolite process, the lime-soda process cannot reduce hardness to zero; it typically leaves a residual hardness of about 50 mg/l.

q: 418. Zeolite process can lower the hardness upto ............
explain: The ion-exchange (zeolite) process is capable of removing almost all calcium and magnesium ions, resulting in 'zero' hardness water.

q: 419. To active the zeolite bed the following is done ............
explain: When the zeolite resin is exhausted, it is 'regenerated' by passing a brine (sodium chloride) solution through it to restore its sodium ions.

q: 420. When the source of water is a reservoir on a mountain slope and the city is in plains then the system of distribution is ............
options: gravity system for a part and pumping for the remaining
explain: A gravity system is used when the source is at a higher elevation than the distribution area, allowing water to flow naturally without pumps.

q: 421. Pumping system is best suited when ............
options: density of population is high and space available is less
source of water is at low level
explain: Direct pumping is often used in high-density urban areas where there is no space for elevated reservoirs or where constant high pressure is required.

q: 422. Combined pumping and gravity flow system is best suited, where ............
options: the city is in plains and source is fairly elevated
the city had a gentle slope and source is elevated
the city is on steep slopes and source is below
explain: A combined system (pumping to a reservoir, then gravity to consumers) is versatile and can be adapted to almost any topographical layout.

q: 423. A disadvantage of combined pumping and gravity flow is that ............
options: it needs pumping round the clock
adequate pressure may not exist in pipes
we may not get enough water to fight fire
explain: The main drawback is the high capital cost and space requirement for constructing elevated storage reservoirs (Overhead Tanks).

q: 424. An advantage of intermittent system of supply of water is ............
options: supply is assured during a fire accident
repairs can be carried out during non-supply hours
explain: In an intermittent system, water is only supplied for a few hours. This allows maintenance crews to perform repairs on pipes during the 'off' hours without wasting water.

q: 425. A major disadvantage of intermittent system of supply of water is ............
options: infiltration of impurities may occur through leaky joints
explain: When the water supply is off, the pressure in the pipes drops. This creates a vacuum that can suck in contaminated groundwater through leaks in the joints.

q: 426. Intermittent system is more popular in Nepal because ............
options: supply hours can be staggered for different zones of different elevations
less quantity of water shall be sufficient
it is highly economical in the long run
explain: Due to the hilly topography and limited water resources, supply is staggered to ensure different zones receive water at specific scheduled times.

q: 427. The purpose of stand pipe is that it ............
options: is of great help in intermittent supply system
explain: Standpipes act as surge tanks or small reservoirs that help maintain and boost hydraulic pressure in the distribution network.

q: 428. Losses in distribution system are due to ............
options: poor quality of pipes and fitting
dead end system of net work of pipes
explain: Physical losses (leaks) are primarily caused by corroded or poor-quality pipe materials and faulty joint fittings.

q: 429. The best material for pipes to be laid under water is ............
explain: Cement concrete pipes are highly durable, do not corrode like metal, and have sufficient weight to remain submerged safely.

q: 430. Mostly used pipe for pumping is ............
explain: Galvanized Iron (GI) pipes are widely used in smaller pumping systems and building plumbing due to their strength and moderate corrosion resistance.

q: 431. The best pipe of water mains known for long life is ............
explain: Cast iron pipes are renowned for their longevity, often lasting over 100 years in certain soil conditions.

q: 432. The pipe that is light, having low coefficient of expansion and resistant to corrosion is ............
explain: Asbestos cement pipes are lightweight compared to iron, have good thermal stability, and are immune to electrochemical corrosion.

q: 433. The only advantage of dead end system is ............
options: it had more number of dead ends
blow of values empty stagnant pocket of water
explain: The dead-end (tree) system requires the least amount of total pipe length, making it the cheapest to install initially.

q: 434. Grid iron system is best suited to ............
options: planned city on a gentle slope
explain: The Grid Iron system follows a rectangular pattern, which is perfectly suited for planned cities with a systematic road network.

q: 435. A disadvantage of interlaced system is ............
explain: In an interlaced or grid system, pipes are connected in loops, which increases the total quantity and length of piping required compared to a tree system.

q: 436. Computations of discharges is difficult for ............
explain: A reticulation (grid) system has many closed loops, making the calculation of flow in each pipe complex (often requiring methods like Hardy Cross).

q: 437. Blow off values are a must when ............
explain: Blow-off valves (scour valves) are placed at dead ends to flush out accumulated sediment and stagnant water.

q: 438. Air valves are provided at ............
explain: Air valves are placed at high points (summits) of the pipeline to release trapped air that could otherwise block the flow of water.

q: 439. Argument against provision of water meters is ............
options: swimming pools have to pay more
sanitation of poor may be neglected
explain: Some argue that if water is metered, poor households might use too little water to save money, potentially leading to poor hygiene and health issues.

q: 440. A goose neck is ............
options: a bent flexible pipe provided between ferrule and stop cock
a T-shaped brass length between water meter and ferrule
a straight G.I. pipe between service pipe and stop cock
a bent rigid pipe between service pipe and water meter
explain: A goose neck is a short, flexible lead or plastic pipe used to connect the service pipe to the main, allowing for small movements without breaking.

q: 441. The valve that is most commonly provided on rising mains is ............
explain: Reflux valves (check valves) are placed on rising mains to prevent the backflow of water to the pump when it stops.

q: 442. Floatation is a process where ............
options: lighter particles are set to float unaided
lighter particles float due to the attachment of gas bubbles
explain: In Dissolved Air Floatation (DAF), tiny gas bubbles attach to solid particles, reducing their density and causing them to float to the surface for removal.

q: 443. Conservation system is best suited ............
explain: The 'Conservancy' (dry) system involves manual collection and removal of waste, which is only economically feasible where labor is very inexpensive.

q: 444. A deplorable aspect of conservancy system is ............
options: vehicles are required to carry night soil
vast areas for disposal are necessary
human elements is involved in collection and transportation of human waste
explain: The most criticized aspect is the 'manual scavenging' or human involvement in handling raw sewage, which is unhygienic and undignified.

q: 445. Water carriage system needs more ............
explain: As the name suggests, the water carriage system uses water as the medium to transport waste through sewers, requiring a significant volume of water to function.

q: 446. Combined system may be favoured where ............
options: rain fall is concentrated in a season of the year and D.W.F. is often fluctuating from day to day
rain fall is scattered throughout the year and D.W.F. is to small compared to storm water
rain fall is distributed throughout the year such that it is <= 10 * D.W.F.
city is on steep rocky slopes
explain: A combined sewer (carrying both sewage and storm water) works best when rainfall is frequent and predictable, keeping the sewers flushed.

q: 447. Separate system is adopted in ............
options: areas where rain fall is distributed throughout the year
explain: In areas with frequent rain, a separate system prevents the treatment plant from being overwhelmed by rainwater while still managing sewage.

q: 448. Partly separate system is ............
options: collecting D.W.F. and storm water in the same sewer
collecting D.W.F. and drainage of initial showers into the same sewer
collection of sewage and sullage into the same sewer
collection of storm water and a part of D.W.F. into the same sewer
explain: This system carries domestic sewage and the highly polluted 'first wash' of storm water in one pipe, while diverting clean excess rain to another.

q: 449. Leaping weir is provided only in ............
explain: A leaping weir is used in combined systems to allow dry weather flow to fall into an intercepting sewer while high-velocity storm water 'leaps' over it.

options: any waste water of domestic or industrial origin
explain: Sewage is the broad term for the liquid waste carried in sewers, originating from residential, commercial, and industrial activities.
Sullage refers specifically to domestic wastewater from kitchens and bathrooms that does not contain human excreta (night soil).

options: collection + conveyance + treatment + ultimate disposal of sewage
explain: Sewerage is the complete science and infrastructure covering the entire path of waste from the point of origin to final disposal.

q: 453. A sanitary sewer is expected to run ............
explain: Sanitary sewers are usually designed to run half-full at maximum discharge to provide space for ventilation and prevent overflows.

q: 454. Top space is left free in a sanitary sewer for ............
explain: Leaving space in the upper part of the pipe allows the system to accommodate sudden increases in flow volume without surging.

q: 455. Maximum flow in sewers may be taken as ............
explain: For design purposes, the peak or maximum flow is typically estimated as three times the average daily flow.

q: 456. In general 'Imperviousness' of any catchment shall be between ............
explain: The runoff coefficient varies based on surface type; a fully paved city might approach 95%, while a park might be as low as 1%.

q: 457. Time of concentration depends on ............
explain: Time of concentration (the time for water to travel from the farthest point to the outlet) is heavily influenced by the slope of the land.

q: 458. Velocity of flow in a sewer should be between ............
explain: Sewers need a 'self-cleansing' velocity of at least 0.6 m/s to prevent settling, but must stay below 3 m/s to prevent erosion of the pipe material.

q: 459. For a partly running circular sewer as the depth of flow increases ............
explain: As the depth of water in a pipe increases (up to a certain point), the cross-sectional area of flow increases, which increases the total discharge (Q).

q: 460. Ovoid sewers are best suited for ............
options: combined system with very wide fluctuations
explain: Ovoid (egg-shaped) sewers maintain a better velocity during low-flow periods (dry weather) compared to circular pipes, making them ideal for systems with high variation.

q: 461. Sewer that collects sewage from toilets is called ............
explain: A lateral sewer is the first stage of the network, collecting sewage directly from individual house connections (toilets/sinks) and carrying it to a branch sewer.

q: 462. The length of the main sewer leading to treatment of disposal units is called ............
explain: The outfall sewer is the final length of the sewerage system that conveys the entire accumulated volume of sewage to the treatment plant or the point of final disposal.

q: 463. A manhole is provided ............
explain: Manholes are essential points of access for inspection and cleaning; they must be placed wherever there is a change in the sewer's alignment, gradient, or pipe diameter.

q: 464. When fall in elevation is greater than 90 cm the manhole provided is called ............
explain: A drop manhole is used when a branch sewer enters a main sewer at a significantly higher elevation, preventing splashing and protecting the manhole structure from erosion.

q: 465. A fight sewer is provided when the gradient is ............
explain: In steep terrain, sewers must follow the slope while maintaining manageable velocities; specialized designs or 'flight' steps are used to manage the energy of the flow.

q: 466. When more than 2 sewers join in a manhole ............
options: their tops should be at the same level
their centres should be that the same level
their bottoms should be at the same level
explain: To maintain a smooth hydraulic profile and prevent backflow under pressure, the soffits (tops) of all incoming pipes should ideally be aligned with the soffit of the outgoing pipe.

q: 467. The working chamber of a manhole, along the direction of flow should have a minimum length of ............
explain: A minimum length of 1.2 m is required to provide enough space for a worker to enter, stand, and use tools comfortably for maintenance.

q: 468. 'Never discharge the contents of a bigger sewer into a smaller though the capacity of the later may be more due to steep slope' because ............
explain: Bigger sewers carry larger solids; if these enter a smaller pipe, they are much more likely to become lodged at the junction or in the pipe, causing a blockage.

q: 469. Before entering a manhole a candle is lowered into the manhole ............
options: to give a signal to the adjacent manhole
to find out presence of oxygen
explain: This is a traditional safety test; if the candle flame goes out, it indicates a lack of oxygen or a high concentration of non-combustible gases like CO2, making it unsafe to enter.

q: 470. A lamphole is helpful in ............
explain: A lamphole allows a light to be lowered into the sewer; by looking through the adjacent manhole, inspectors can check for obstructions or misalignments in the pipe.

q: 471. A syphon spillway is an arrangement to ............
options: divert excessive D.W.F. into open drain
divert excessive storm water into drain
divert excessive combine flow water into drain
explain: In combined systems, syphon spillways act as automatic relief valves to divert excess water (mixture of sewage and storm water) to a nearby watercourse during heavy rain.

q: 472. Colour of fresh sewage is ............
explain: Fresh sewage is typically a light grey or soapy color. As it becomes 'stale' or septic over time, it turns dark grey and eventually black.

q: 473. The best pH range suited for most of bacteria is ............
explain: Most biological treatment processes rely on bacteria that thrive in a near-neutral to slightly alkaline environment, generally between pH 5 and 9.

q: 474. The bacteria that flourish at high temperature (greater than 45°C) are called ............
explain: Thermophilic bacteria are 'heat-loving' organisms used in high-temperature sludge digestion processes to speed up decomposition.

q: 475. Aerobic bacteria ............
options: produce less energy and more end products
explain: Aerobic bacteria require dissolved oxygen to survive; movement (aeration) keeps oxygen levels high, whereas stagnant water quickly becomes depleted of oxygen.

q: 476. Anaerobes give out ............
explain: Anaerobic decomposition is less efficient than aerobic; it produces unstable intermediate compounds like organic acids and gases (CH4, H2S) that are highly odorous.

q: 477. The common end products for both aerobiosis and anaerobiosis is ............
explain: Carbon dioxide is the ultimate stable oxidized form of carbon and is released in both types of biological decomposition.

q: 478. A unit working purely on anaerobiosis is ............
explain: A septic tank is an enclosed, airtight chamber where solids settle and undergo anaerobic digestion without the presence of dissolved oxygen.

q: 479. Anaerobic treatment is best suited for ............
explain: Anaerobic processes (like sludge digesters) are ideal for concentrated organic waste because they don't require the massive energy input of aeration needed for aerobic treatment.

q: 480. A natural method of disposal of sewage is ............
explain: Applying sewage directly to land (irrigation) uses the natural filtering capacity of soil and biological action of soil microbes to treat the waste.

q: 481. Sewage farming is best suited for Nepal because ............
options: it is a cheap method of sewage disposal
nutrients and trace elements required by plants are available in sewage
explain: Sewage contains Nitrogen, Phosphorus, and Potassium (NPK). In agricultural regions, this 'liquid fertilizer' provides essential nutrients for crop growth.

q: 482. Sewage sickness is a sickness developed by ............
options: humans due to consumption of crops grown on sewage
plants because to harmful elements of sewage irrigation
land unable to accept any more loading of sewage
sewage itself due to pathogens within
explain: If too much sewage is applied to land without rest, the soil pores become clogged (anaerobic), preventing air from reaching roots and causing the land to become 'sick' and unproductive.

q: 483. An ideal crop of sewage irrigation is ............
explain: Crops like bananas are ideal because the edible part is high above the ground and protected by a skin, minimizing health risks compared to root vegetables or low-lying greens.

q: 484. When raw sewage is to be disposed off by dilution sewage should ............
options: be having a B.O.D. less than 150 mg/l
explain: Floating matter (grease, plastics, corks) creates an immediate aesthetic nuisance in rivers or lakes, so these must be removed via screening before dilution.

q: 485. Self-purification of a stream is quite rapid when ............
options: course is full of rapids and waterfalls
explain: Rapids and waterfalls create turbulence, which rapidly increases the rate of 're-aeration' (dissolving atmospheric oxygen into the water) to speed up biological oxidation.

q: 486. Coarse screens are iron bars with a clearance of ............
explain: Coarse screens (rack screens) typically have spacing between 25mm and 75mm to catch large debris like rags, wood, and stones.

q: 487. Grit chamber had a detention period of ............
explain: Grit chambers are designed to remove heavy inorganic solids very quickly (usually in about 60 seconds) before they can reach and damage downstream pumps or treatment units.

q: 488. Velocity of flow through a grit chamber is ............
explain: The velocity is kept low enough (approx 0.3 m/s) to allow sand and grit to settle, but high enough to keep organic matter in suspension.

q: 489. Grit obtained in a grit chamber is used ............
explain: Because grit is largely composed of inorganic sand and gravel, it can be washed and reused in construction or as a fill material.

q: 490. The factor governing the detention period in a grit chamber is ............
explain: The detention time is calculated based on how long it takes for a particle to travel the length of the chamber at a specific horizontal flow velocity.

q: 491. The factor deciding the length of a grit chamber is ............
explain: The length of the chamber is the product of the horizontal velocity and the required detention time for the smallest target particle to settle.

q: 492. 'Mass action' during sedimentation is the property of ............
options: settling of a particle along with the neighbouring particle
explain: In hindered or zone settling, particles are so concentrated that they settle as a single mass or 'blanket' rather than individually.

q: 493. Overflow rat of for primary clarifier is ............
explain: Primary clarifiers are typically designed with an overflow rate (surface loading) in the range of 20 to 30 cubic meters per square meter per day.

q: 494. B.O.D. removal of primary clarifier is ............
explain: Primary sedimentation removes 50-70% of suspended solids, which usually corresponds to a 30-40% reduction in the total Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD).

q: 495. A fundamental difference between sedimentation tank for water and sewage is ............
options: sewage sedimentation tanks have more depth
sludge from sewage sedimentation is to be removed more frequently
it can be final treatment of operation in water treatment
explain: In water treatment, sedimentation might be the final step before disinfection; in sewage treatment, it is almost always just a preliminary step before biological oxidation.

q: 496. Sedimentation aided by coagulation is rarely done for sanitary sewage because ............
options: time of treatment is further prolonged
sludge cannot be disposed of easily
chemicals may be harmful to living organisms of sewage
explain: Chemical coagulation produces a very large volume of sludge that is often difficult to dewater and digest compared to purely biological sludge.

q: 497. Sedimentation aided by coagulation is adopted ............
options: where biological treatment is to follow next
when industrial wastes are blended with sanitary sewage
when phosphates are less in sewage
explain: Coagulation is necessary when dealing with complex industrial effluents (dyes, chemicals) that wouldn't settle under gravity alone.

q: 498. A septic tank is a water tight tank where the following operation(s) take place ............
options: decomposition of organic and inorganic matter by bacteria
explain: Septic tanks provide two-stage treatment: first, solids settle (sedimentation), and second, the settled solids are broken down by bacteria in the absence of air (anaerobic digestion).

q: 499. Mostly adopted detention period for a septic tank is ............
explain: A 24-hour detention period is the standard design to ensure adequate time for both settling and the start of biological activity.

q: 500. The gases given out of a septic tank are ............
explain: Anaerobic digestion produces a mixture of Carbon Dioxide, Methane (fuel gas), and Hydrogen Sulphide (the source of the smell).
